keyVerseText: Two and twenty years old was Ahaziah when he began to reign; and he reigned one year in Jerusalem. And his mother's name was Athaliah, the daughter of Omri king of Israel. daughter: or, granddaughter
rootMeaning: The root of עֲתַלְיָה (ʻĂthalyâh) derives from עַתְלַי (ʻAthlay), which means "whom Jehovah afflicts," combined with יָהּ (Yah), a shortened form of the divine name Yahweh. This etymology suggests a meaning along the lines of "Jah has constrained" or "afflicted of the Lord," indicating a personal name that carries the weight of divine discipline or testing. This literal sense goes beyond a mere proper noun, pointing to a character marked by God's sovereign involvement, whether in judgment or refining.
usageInScripture: The name Athaliah appears 17 times in Scripture, predominantly as a proper noun referring to a specific Israelite woman and two men. The top translations consistently render the name as "Athaliah" or phrases incorporating it, such as "and Athaliah" or "of Athaliah," showing a consistent recognition of the name as a distinct individual. This usage highlights the name's role primarily as a personal identifier, most notably that of the daughter of Ahab and Jezebel and mother of Ahaziah, whose narrative is marked by significant and tragic events in Judah's royal history.
theologicalSignificance: Understanding the name Athaliah as "afflicted of the Lord" or "Jah has constrained" deepens our grasp of God's sovereign hand even in the lives of those who oppose Him. Athaliah's story, tied to judgment and violence, reflects the reality that divine discipline can manifest in ways that test faithfulness and reveal the consequences of rebellion. For the Christian faith, this underscores God's authority over history and individuals, reminding believers that God's purposes prevail through both blessing and affliction. It also points to the hope that God's constraints are ultimately redemptive, shaping His covenant people according to His will.
keyVerseReflection: 2 Kings 8:26 states, "Two and twenty years old was Ahaziah when he began to reign... And his mother's name was Athaliah, the daughter of Omri king of Israel." Here, the name Athaliah situates Ahaziah's lineage within a complex royal and spiritual context. The name's meaning, "afflicted of the Lord," adds a layer of significance to this identification, hinting at the divine judgment and turmoil surrounding this family line. It reminds readers that Ahaziah's reign and the legacy of Athaliah are intertwined with God's sovereign purposes and the unfolding of His redemptive history.
